import sys
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
import stackd_search_windows_probe as p
from pathlib import Path

p.cap['sources'].append({'path': __file__, 'content': Path(__file__).read_text()})
p.guard('boundaries')
for scan in ['TimestampAscending','TimestampDescending']:
    for budget in [4,5,7,9,11]:
        p.query('allocation-search-two-'+scan+'-max-'+str(budget), [p.expr(p.search(2))], budget, scan)
    for budget in [4,5,7,8,17,18]:
        p.query('allocation-mixed-three-'+scan+'-max-'+str(budget), [p.direct(),p.expr(p.search(2))], budget, scan)
    for budget in [5,6]:
        p.query('completion-search-one-'+scan+'-max-'+str(budget), [p.expr(p.search())], budget, scan)
    p.query('completion-hidden-unused-'+scan+'-max-18',[p.direct(),p.expr(p.search(2),'hidden',ReturnData=False)],18,scan)
    for budget in [1,2,3,4,5,8]:
        p.query('short-search-two-'+scan+'-max-'+str(budget),[p.expr(p.search(2))],budget,scan,start=0,end=240)
    for budget in [1,2]:
        p.query('empty-search-one-'+scan+'-max-'+str(budget),[p.expr(p.search())],budget,scan,start=240,end=360)
        p.query('empty-direct-one-'+scan+'-max-'+str(budget),[p.direct()],budget,scan,start=240,end=360)
p.query('allocation-hidden-search-visible-sum-max-5',[p.expr(p.search(2),'hidden',ReturnData=False),p.expr('SUM(hidden)')],5)
p.query('allocation-visible-search-visible-sum-max-5',[p.expr(p.search(2),'visible'),p.expr('SUM(visible)')],5)
p.query('allocation-hidden-direct-unused-max-2',[p.direct(),p.direct(1,True)],2)
p.query('allocation-hidden-direct-unused-max-3',[p.direct(),p.direct(1,True)],3)
p.query('fraction-truncated-budget-60.5-max-3',[p.expr(p.search(1,60.5))],3)
p.query('fraction-truncated-budget-120.5-max-2',[p.expr(p.search(1,120.5))],2)

import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import types
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
fixture = json.loads(Path('testdata/aws/cloudwatch/metric_search_windows.json').read_text())
probe_source = next(s['content'] for s in fixture['sources'] if s['path'] == '/tmp/stackd_search_windows_probe.py')
namespace = {'__file__': __file__, '__name__': 'embedded_window_probe'}
exec(compile(probe_source, '<embedded_window_probe>', 'exec'), namespace)
p = types.SimpleNamespace(**namespace)
p.guard('generated')
for scan in ['TimestampAscending', 'TimestampDescending']:
    for budget in [1,2]:
        p.query('generated-time-series-'+scan+'-max-'+str(budget),[p.expr('TIME_SERIES(7)',Period=60)],budget,scan)
        p.query('generated-fill-hidden-direct-'+scan+'-max-'+str(budget),[p.direct(0,True),p.expr('FILL(m1,0)',Period=60)],budget,scan)
    for budget in [1,2,3,5,9]:
        second = p.direct(1)
        second['MetricStat']['Period'] = 120
        p.query('mixed-period-direct-60-120-'+scan+'-max-'+str(budget),[p.direct(0),second],budget,scan)

primary_reference_details.relevance: Documents MaxDatapoints, exclusive EndTime, ScanBy ordering and native NextToken continuation; does not specify the measured sparse-slot allocation rule.
Documents Complete/PartialData and explicitly says NextToken is not returned when performing a math expression.
Documents exact MetricName/Namespace selectors and SUM(SEARCH(...)); fractional period conversion and slot allocation below are native measurements, not documented promises.

measured_behavior.observed: The exact selectors return only SDBFailure (Sum 212 at anchor, 220 at anchor+120) and Network-Errors_2 (252 at anchor, 264 at anchor+180). The main window [anchor-60,anchor+300) contains six 60-second slots: a leading empty slot, interior gaps, and a trailing empty slot. Short controls use [anchor,anchor+240), and empty controls use [anchor+240,anchor+360). SEARCH pair order is Network-Errors_2 then SDBFailure; direct pair order follows the submitted m1=SDBFailure,m2=Network-Errors_2 controls.

Measured positive fractional periods behave as truncation to the integer part before integer validation: 0.5 gives the zero-period error; 1.5,5.5,30.5,60.5,60.9,120.5 succeed and exactly match their integer controls; 2.5 and 59.5 give the allowed-small-period-set error; 61.5 and 119.9 give the multiple-of-60 error. Integral 2,6,31,59 fail the small-period set rule. Raw native validation strings and newlines are retained in output/raw_response.

Query Period supplies an omitted SEARCH period. Explicit SEARCH 60.5 overrides query Period 120 and returns anchor/anchor+120; explicit 120.5 overrides query Period 60 and buckets the known samples at anchor-60/anchor+60 in this window, exactly as integral 120. Fractional 60.5 with budget 3 remains partial after three 60-second slots; 120.5 with budget 2 returns both known points but remains partial because the third 120-second slot is unprocessed.

Empty slots consume budget. At budget 1 the six-slot direct window takes six native-token pages even though only two pages contain datapoints. Both scan directions traverse their respective dense slots, retaining empty pages. SEARCH remains PartialData at budget 5 even when both known values are returned, and becomes Complete at budget 6. An entirely empty two-slot window is PartialData at budget 1 and Complete at budget 2; direct retrieval has a real second page, while SEARCH has no token.

For the equal-period sources and aligned windows tested, the coherent allocation model reserves q=floor(B/N) dense slots per underlying source, then spends the entire remainder B-N*q on the earliest source, spilling to the next only when the earlier source's window is exhausted. This is neither actual-point budgeting nor round-robin remainder distribution. Two sources at B=3 receive [2,1], B=7 gives [4,3], and B=11 gives [6,5]. Three sources at B=4 receive [2,1,1], B=5 gives [3,1,1], B=8 gives [4,2,2], and B=17 gives [6,6,5]. B<N can leave later sources with zero allocation: mixed B=2 processes the first direct source's first two slots, whereas B=3 allocates one slot to every source and therefore returns less visible data in this leading-empty window. Scan direction changes which end of each source is consumed, not the allocation order.
measured_behavior.prior_fixture_agreement: The same model explains metric_search.json control-page-59: twelve five-slot sources reserve four each, then the eleven-slot remainder fills the first eleven sources to five slots; the final source stays partial. page-5-TimestampAscending reserves zero each and spends all five slots on the first source.

measured_behavior.observed: Two SEARCH matches consume two source allocations even when ReturnData=false and only SUM is visible. Inline SUM(SEARCH(...)), hidden SEARCH plus SUM, and visible SEARCH plus SUM preserve the source budget; the derived output is not an additional source allocation. Referenced hidden direct metrics also count. Direct SDBFailure plus SEARCH selecting SDBFailure and Network-Errors_2 consumes three source allocations, not two deduplicated metric identities; all complete only at 18 slots in this window. An UNUSED hidden SEARCH still counts its expanded sources and suppresses NextToken. In contrast, an UNUSED hidden direct MetricStat is pruned: the visible direct metric gets the whole budget and follows the same three pages at B=2 or two pages at B=3 as the standalone direct control. Hidden-source pruning therefore cannot be generalized across direct and SEARCH queries.

TIME_SERIES(7) alone with query Period=60 returns all six dense slots Complete at MaxDatapoints=1 and 2, in both requested scan orders, without messages or token. Thus these requests have no generated-output cap or measured retrieval-source cost. FILL(hidden direct,0) instead exposes only the allocated source window: ascending B=1 returns [anchor-60]=[0], B=2 returns [anchor-60,anchor]=[0,212]; descending B=1 returns [anchor+240]=[0], B=2 returns [anchor+240,anchor+180]=[0,0]. All four FILL results are PartialData with the exact Paginated-derived message and no token. Missing data outside the allocated source window is not filled across the rest of the request.

The same aligned six-minute request has six slots for direct SDBFailure at Period=60 and three slots for direct Network-Errors_2 at Period=120. The latter's known values are bucketed at anchor-60 and anchor+180. In both scan directions, budgets 1,2,3,5,9 exhaust in respectively 9,5,3,2,1 native pages. B=1 consumes all six first-source slots before the second source gets data. B=2 initially gives each source one slot of its own period, so the second source returns a value while the first source's leading/trailing minute is empty; after three pages the second source completes and later pages contain only the first source. B=3 initially allocates two 60-second slots and one 120-second slot, and both sources complete on page three. This supports dense slots per source's own period, not a common time horizon or elapsed-seconds budget, for this mixed-period pair.

SEARCH members have individual Complete/PartialData statuses; a complete member has no Messages property, while a partial member has Code=PartialData and Value="The expression may contain partial data as one or more metrics have StatusCode 'Paginated'". Reduced SUM is partial when any required source is partial, and computes from available values rather than waiting for complete sources: at B=3 its ascending anchor value is 252 rather than the complete sum 464. Direct partial results have no per-result message. All measured SEARCH/math requests omit NextToken, including mixed direct plus SEARCH and unused hidden SEARCH; top-level Messages is empty. Direct-only requests preserve native NextToken until exhaustion. In the two-direct B=3 chain the first metric becomes complete on page three and is absent from page four, which finishes the other metric. Tokens are copied verbatim into the next request; their encoding or semantic contents are not inferred.

allocation_model.scope: Measured aligned, recent source retrieval: 60-second two/four/six-slot windows; a mixed direct pair with six 60-second slots and three 120-second slots; singleton 120-second fractional controls; and standalone generated TIME_SERIES plus FILL of a hidden direct source.
first_page: Determine underlying retrieval sources, not merely visible output count: expand SEARCH matches, retain referenced direct dependencies, retain even unused SEARCH expansions, prune unused hidden direct MetricStat.
Order observed sources as direct retrievals before SEARCH expansions; the two selected SEARCH members have distinct lexical labels, so no tie-break is inferred.

For N>0 let B=MaxDatapoints, N=number of retrieval sources, q=floor(B/N). Reserve min(q,remaining_dense_slots) for each source, then assign B minus the total reservation in source order, capped by each source's remaining dense slots. Each source's dense slots use its own Period.

Consume each source's allocated slots from the ScanBy end of its own window, including empty slots; emit only the actual datapoints. A source remains partial until all its dense slots have been processed.

Evaluate expressions using available source datapoints and propagate partial source status. Visible derived outputs do not consume another retrieval allocation. FILL of the tested hidden source fills only its allocated window. For N=0 the tested TIME_SERIES(7) creates all six requested slots Complete without applying MaxDatapoints as an output cap.
allocation_model.continuation_evidence: All native direct NextTokens were followed through exhaustion. Direct controls are consistent with continuing each source from its own consumed dense-slot position, removing exhausted sources on later pages. This is a behavioral model, not a decoding or invention of token contents.

unresolved_boundaries: The aligned direct 60/120-second pair agrees with per-source slot allocation. Other mixed periods, SEARCH mixed-period arrays, retention tiers, and unaligned/subsecond request boundaries remain unmeasured; the model is not asserted universally across those boundaries.
Only positive fractional SEARCH literals were measured here. Negative fractional values, exponent/overflow extremes, and nonnumeric expression-valued periods are outside this conversion evidence.
The selected series have distinct default labels. Stable ordering of equal labels, arbitrary multi-expression interleaving, and cross-account retrieval remain outside this capture.
Unused hidden SEARCH and unused hidden direct MetricStat behave differently in measured controls. No broader optimizer pruning rule is claimed for other metric-math functions.
Direct continuation tokens are opaque service data. No token format, lifetime, portability, or mutation behavior was tested or inferred.
